text:
Marathon Petroleum stock rose 0.4% today to $399.41, continuing a strong two-week rally of over 12%. The move reflects crude oil prices climbing sharply—Brent crude topped $101 per barrel for the first time since July as escalating U.S.-Iran tensions and military strikes in the Persian Gulf sparked concern over potential disruptions to Middle East energy supplies. Refineries are running at 98% capacity with tight inventory levels across gasoline and diesel, which amplifies the benefit to refiners when crude costs rise faster than product prices.

The broader tailwind here is that oil refining operates on the spread between what they pay for crude and what they sell refined products for—when crude prices spike on geopolitical risk but refined product demand and pricing don't fall equally fast, refiners' profit margins expand. With refineries already running near full capacity and storage levels lean, MPC is positioned to capture more of these margin gains as the region remains unstable.
